blocks.text: These are small molecules derived from a single amino acid (usually Tyrosine or Tryptophan). Their ability to pass through cell membranes depends on whether they behave more like a protein or more like a lipid. Epinephrine and norepinephrine cannot cross membranes while thyroxine and tri-iodothyronine can cross. Examples include;

blocks.title: Tidbit
blocks.text: In 1902, two British scientists, Bayliss and Starling, discovered hormone during their research on digestive system. They found that when acidic gastric juice comes in small intestine, a substance (which they called “secretin”) was released into blood. Secretin reaches the pancreas and stimulates it to secrete pancreatic juice.
